overview: South of the Middle Lands, behind a belt of storms that kept the explorers of the First Age out and an inland heat that kills, lie the Ember Lands: a volcanic island of grey plateau and burning ridges, the forested peninsula of Mirolon on the southern neck of the central landmass, a scatter of storm-beaten isles, and in the far south the Nether, the seat of the King of Demons. Volgan, the Great Spirit and principal dark lord, rules the island from Nafeher through his necromantic orders and grave hosts, with orcs, ogres, goblins and devils among his soldiers and three demon realms sworn to him as the Southern Dominion. Mirolon, the human realm he conquered in the First Age and lost after Dardan, keeps its beacons lit toward the south; the salt freeholds of Halia, the warlord of Nan and the shrine-isle of Olen live between the two by paying tolls and saying nothing; the Nether keeps its own counsel behind the Sea of Lava, and its king's pacts bind the living while the dead remain Zol's; and at the east tip of the island a chasm drops into the Abyss, where Roka once held a necklace that a thief carried away to the north. In 4A 1748 almost nobody outside Mirolon believes the island is anything but a spent legend. The sworn realms count by the Musters of the Dominion and the Nether by the years of its pacts; the men of the peninsula keep the Reckoning of the Twelve. Years are one continuous count from the victory of Aen: 1A 1 is year 1, the First Age runs to 1675, the Second Age from 1676 (2A 1) to 3808 (2A 2133), the Third Age from 3809 (3A 1) to 5068 (3A 1260, the proposed length) and the Fourth Age from 5069 (4A 1), so that the campaign year 4A 1748 is 6816; a founding year of 0 marks a realm older than the numbered years, whose beginning nobody dates. Everything here that the vault does not state is proposed.

ages.name: The Storm-Bound Age
ages.summary: Storms at sea and a killing heat keep the explorers of Aenor away from the island, and men chart its coasts without knowing what lies behind them. On the peninsula, Ainic lake-folk found the kingdom of Mirolon around its lake, and their coast cousins boil salt on the shore of Veleeda.

ages.name: Volgan's War
ages.summary: In the second millennium of the First Age Volgan invades Mirolon and makes it the opening of a vast campaign against Aenor, with demons, devils, orcs, goblins and dragons in his hosts. He is banished to the Void after Dardan, and Elzon holds the Ember Lands against the Grand Alliance's invasion and drives it back with heavy losses.

ages.name: The Age of the Necromancer
ages.summary: Elzon, the Great Necromancer, rules the Ember Lands from Nazerun and wages a long war of raids against Aenor; demons come out of the Nether through portals, and the Burning Gate of Nezer is closed by men, elves and Dark Lands soldiers. Elzon brings back Volgan's presence from the Void and in 2A 2133 takes Aenor.

ages.name: The Long Weakness
ages.summary: While Elzon rules Aenor, Volgan is too weak to leave the Ember Lands and gives his orders from Nafeher; the island's magic sustains the necromancers as Aenor's does not. Mirolon pays a silent toll to the Necromancer's order, the portals close one by one, and the age ends with Elzon's permanent death.

countries.name: Puvulan

founding.story: The necromantic orders call the grey plateau of the island Puvulan, the dust fields, and the Dominion that rules it is older than any chronicle of men. Nobody in Aoaz knows how the Great Spirit Volgan came to hold the plateau or when he raised the gate of Nafeher; the orders' own rolls begin with his name and admit no earlier one.

roots.story: Puvulan is the realm of a power, and its roots are the power's own. Long before Aen, Volgan was the servant of a New God, overcame that god and founded his own dominion; which god, and when, nobody in Aoaz knows. The necromantic orders that serve him on the grey plateau teach that Nafeher's gate was the first thing raised on the dust fields, before the orders, before the grave-fields and before any living thing that now serves there; their rolls begin with his name and admit no earlier one, and how the Great Spirit came to hold the plateau is not written in them. The orders' customs grow from the gate. Whoever passes through it to serve the Dominion has his name cut in the ring of names round the gateway, and the dead of the grave hosts are raised under the names of those who served before them; offices are given in the Rite-Tongue; the Musters, not months, measure the year; and a servant who betrays the Dominion has his name cut out of the ring, which the orders hold to be worse than death. The First Age made the gate known beyond the plateau. The Kalioth kings paid it the Black Tribute and marched with Volgan to Dardan, his fleets crossed the Sound to take Mirolon in 1A 1150, and demons, devils, orcs, goblins and dragons marched under it. After Dardan Volgan was cast into the Void and Elzon governed in his name; the Necromancer brought his presence back in 2A 1544 and served him until his own death in 3A 1260. Since then the Dominion has been rebuilt behind the Veil of Storms, the demon realms have sworn to the gate, and the ring of names has begun to fill again.

sign.device: The Gate of Nafeher: a plain upright gateway in bone white standing within a plain ring of bone white, on grave black.
sign.origin: The gate is Volgan's own sign, as old as his dominion on the plateau, and it appears on no other banner of Aoaz. The ring round it is the ring of names cut round the gateway, in which every servant of the Dominion is written; on the banners it is shown plain, because the names are spoken in the Rite-Tongue and never sewn. The grave hosts carried the gate at the taking of Miherta in 1A 1150 and at Dardan, Elzon's orders carried it through the Second and Third Ages in Volgan's name, and the sworn realms of the Southern Dominion fly their own banners beneath it.
sign.meaning: Whoever passes through the gate belongs to it: to the orders and the sworn realms the promise that service is remembered in the ring, and to every living realm the threat that the dead will march under it again.

dynasties.name: The Dominion of Nafeher
dynasties.notable: Volgan rules in person through his lieutenants, the necromantic orders and the officers of the grave hosts, whose titles are written in the Rite-Tongue; in his absence in the Second and Third Ages, Elzon governed in his name.

events.name: The Invasion of Mirolon
events.summary: Volgan crosses Mirolon Sound with fleets that the storms do not hinder, takes the lake-kingdom of Mirolon and makes it the opening of his war on Aenor.

events.name: Dardan and the Defence of the Island
events.summary: By the end of the First Age the Grand Alliance breaks Volgan's host at Dardan and spirits cast him into the Void; Elzon withdraws the remnants to the island and drives back the Alliance's invasion with heavy losses.

events.name: The Return from the Void
events.summary: After centuries of work Elzon brings Volgan's presence back from the Void with old death-magic; Volgan returns without his former strength and gives his servant a freer hand.

events.name: The Death of the Necromancer
events.summary: Elzon dies in Aenor and does not return, and Volgan, still too weak to leave the Ember Lands, loses his greatest servant and the conquered crownlands of the north.

events.name: The Southern Dominion Sworn
events.summary: As Volgan's strength returns, the demon realms of Khorvrath, Dolon and Nezer swear to Nafeher, and the Dominion strikes its first bargain of the age with the Nether.

events.name: The Veil of Storms
events.summary: The necromantic orders thicken the storms of the Tempest Reach round the island, so that the few ships that come near see only weather and the courts of the north see nothing at all.

countries.capitalReason: Nafeher stands on the grey plateau behind the storms, far from any shore a fleet could reach and on ground no army can feed, and Volgan's gate has stood there since before men kept records.
countries.today: In 4A 1748, in the Musters that the Dominion counts instead of months, Volgan rules the plateau, the Demonic Mountains, the Abyss's rim, Unlo and the isle of Exhoros from Nafeher, with some 300,000 living subjects among orcs, ogres, goblins and men of the plateau oases, and the dead uncounted. Behind the Veil of Storms the Dominion has spent a century filling its musters again, which only Mirolon's scouts believe; the sworn demon realms keep their oaths, Dolon's forges make black powder for the orc companies, and the border at the Nether Maw is disputed with the King of Demons.

divergence.what: Volgan keeps the veil closed and never strikes first.
divergence.consequence: The south stays at peace through the War of the Last Crowns, the Middle Lands face only the West, the East and the dead, and the Dominion grows unseen.

divergence.what: Volgan turns first on the Dark Lands holds instead of marching on Mirolon.
divergence.consequence: Goldoroth and the orc holds kneel or fight, the Dominion grows by subjects rather than by conquest, and Mirolon gains years to prove its warning.

countries.name: Mirolon

founding.story: The old lake-kingdom of Mirolon, founded by Ainic lake-folk around its lake in the First Age, lost its kings when Volgan took Miherta. When his host collapsed after Dardan the survivors came back from the swamps and the hills, and in 2A 3 the pass-lords and the lake towns chose Hadric of Miherta to watch the south for life, the first High Warden of a realm that would never again trust a single royal line.

roots.story: Mirolon was a lake-kingdom before it was a watch. Ainic lake-folk founded it on its lake and the peninsula's north shore in 1A 377, their speech became the southern daughter of Old Ainic, and the lake-kings built Miherta's beacon tower to guide boats home across the lake, not to watch the south. In 1A 1150 Volgan crossed the Sound with fleets the storms did not hinder, took Miherta and killed the last lake-king, and Mirolon became the opening of his war on Aenor. The survivors went into the Great Swamp and the hills and stayed there for more than five centuries. The swamp years made the wardens: the hidden villages learned to read Volgan's patrols by the herons of the swamp, which rose when strangers came and stood still when the reeds were empty, and the watchers who stood night after night as still as the herons became the first scouts. When Volgan's host broke at Dardan and his garrisons starved, the survivors came back out of the swamp, and in 2A 3 the pass-lords and the lake towns chose Hadric of Miherta to watch the south for life. He refused to wear the lake-kings' crown and hung it in the beacon tower instead, and Mirolon has never again trusted a single royal line. From the swamp years and from Hadric come the wardens' laws: every tower keeps a lamp lit toward the south each night; a warden who lets his lamp go out is struck from the rolls; the High Warden is elected for life and may not pass the office to a child; and the crown stays in the beacon tower.

sign.device: A grey heron standing upright with its neck drawn back, watchful, in heron grey and white on night blue.
sign.origin: The heron is the watcher of the swamp years, the bird whose rising warned the hidden villages of Volgan's patrols and whose stillness told them the reeds were empty. Hadric's scouts sewed it on the reed-cloth they carried out of the Great Swamp after Dardan, and the High Wardens have flown it since 2A 3 over Miherta's beacon tower, where the lake-kings' crown hangs unworn.
sign.meaning: The watch that never sleeps: to the peninsula a promise that the towers are manned every night, and to Nafeher the warning that nothing crosses the Sound unseen.

dynasties.name: The Lake-Kings of Mirolon
dynasties.notable: The Ainic line that founded the lake-kingdom and ended when Volgan took Miherta in 1A 1150; the wardens keep its crown in the beacon tower and do not wear it.

dynasties.name: The High Wardens
dynasties.notable: Each High Warden is elected for life by the pass-lords and the lake towns, man or woman, and leads the scouts in war; Mirena of the Passes has been High Warden since 4A 1739.

events.name: The Lake-Kingdom
events.summary: Ainic lake-folk found the kingdom of Mirolon on the lake and the peninsula's north shore, and their speech becomes the southern daughter of Old Ainic.

events.name: The Fall of Miherta
events.summary: Volgan crosses the Sound, takes Miherta and kills the last lake-king, and Mirolon becomes the opening of his campaign against Aenor.

events.name: The Herons of the Swamp
events.summary: In the Great Swamp, where the survivors of Miherta hide from Volgan's garrisons, the hidden villages learn to read the patrols by the rising of the herons, and the still watchers become the first scouts of Mirolon.

events.name: The Freeing of the Peninsula
events.summary: When Volgan's host breaks at Dardan his garrisons on the peninsula starve or flee, and the Grand Alliance stages its failed invasion of the island from Mirolon's shore.

events.name: The First Beacon
events.summary: The wardens begin to keep a lamp lit toward the south in every tower; they say the first was lit by a child who saw the storms part in the wrong direction.

events.name: The Silent Toll
events.summary: With Aenor fallen, Mirolon pays a yearly toll to the Necromancer's order rather than be taken again, and the wardens keep their towers manned through twelve centuries of paying it.

events.name: The Fortifying of the Passes
events.summary: Scouts report that the storms round the island have changed, and the High Warden fortifies the northern passes of the land neck and the beacon line along the Sound.

events.name: The Envoy Laughed At
events.summary: Mirolon's envoy Baelan of Paron warns the court at Parim that the Ember Lands are arming; the court laughs, saying Volgan has been quiet for longer than Aenor has had kings.

countries.capitalReason: Miherta stands on the lake and the peninsula's north shore, the seat of the old lake-kings, from whose beacon tower the wardens can see both the land neck and the storm line of the Sound.
countries.today: High Warden Mirena of the Passes rules the peninsula north of the Nan Mountains, its forests, its lake and the Great Swamp from Miherta, some 800,000 wardens, farmers and reed-cutters. Mirolon is free, watchful and alone: its scouts take the signs from the south seriously, Parim laughed at its envoy twelve years ago, and the beacon towers are manned every night.

divergence.what: Mirolon holds its passes and its shore when the Dominion comes.
divergence.consequence: The march north is delayed or broken, the Middle Lands gain a year or more, and the Children of Volgan grow less likely.

divergence.what: Mirolon falls and its court goes into exile in the Zilin Hills or among the marches of Herez.
divergence.consequence: A warden-court without land carries the only first-hand knowledge of the Dominion north, and its scouts become the eyes of whoever shelters them.

countries.name: Khorvrath

founding.story: In the years when portals opened across Aoaz, a demon house came up out of the Nether Maw onto the island's Nether foothills with its thralls and would not go back down. It raised the horn-hold of Khorvazel in the hills, took the name Khorvrath, the horn-realm, and kept the pact-name of its lord to itself.

roots.story: Khorvrath's lords are older than their realm by more than anyone among men can count. Demons are corrupted angels, immortal Great Folk, and the house that became Khorvrath was one of the houses of the Nether's Halls under the King of Demons, a house of beast-breeders whose great horned beasts drew the lava-sledges of the Halls and carried its lords to war. The houses compete for the king's favour and the right to open portals, and Khorvrath's house lost that contest: in the years when portals opened across Aoaz it was refused a portal of its own, and in 2A 977 it came up out of the Nether Maw onto the island's foothills with its thralls and its beasts and would not go back down. The first lord rode out of the Maw on the greatest of the house's beasts and broke one of its horns on the rim of the vent, and the house took the broken horn as proof that the way back was closed behind it. From the Maw come the horned court's customs: its lords keep a name of two beats for the world and a pact-name for the court; the hall of Khorvazel, cut into the foothills by thralls in 2A 1002, is crowned with the horns of the house's beasts, one for every lord and every great servant who has fallen; and no lord of the house goes back down into the Maw. The house fought at the Burning Gate of Nezer and lost its lord when men, elves and Dark Lands soldiers closed it in 2A 1388, and in 4A 1650 it swore to Volgan, trading its freedom from the Nether's houses for a place in his hosts.

sign.device: A single great curved horn broken off at its tip, in ember gold on ash black.
sign.origin: The broken horn is the horn the first lord broke on the rim of the Nether Maw when the house rode out in 2A 977, and it is set above the horn-seat of Khorvazel. The house's companies carried it at the Burning Gate in 2A 1388, and since the oath to Nafeher in 4A 1650 they have carried it beneath the Gate of Nafeher in the Dominion's musters, the only horned banner of the island.
sign.meaning: No way back down: to the thralls and the companies a promise that the house will never return them to the Halls, to the Nether's houses a challenge, and to Olen the reminder that the horned court forgets nothing it has lost.

dynasties.name: The Horned Court
dynasties.notable: A demon lordship whose lords keep a name of two beats for the world and a pact-name for the court; the lord of Khorvrath is Morvath, who took the horn-seat after his predecessor fell at the Burning Gate of Nezer.

events.name: Out of the Maw
events.summary: A demon house climbs out of the Nether Maw onto the foothills with its thralls and founds the horned court of Khorvrath.

events.name: The Horn-Hold Raised
events.summary: Thralls cut the hall of Khorvazel into the foothills, a hold of black stone crowned with the horns of the house's beasts.

events.name: The Burning Gate
events.summary: Khorvrath's companies fight beside other demons at the Burning Gate of Nezer and lose their lord when men, elves and Dark Lands soldiers close it.

events.name: Sworn to Nafeher
events.summary: Khorvrath swears to Volgan as a realm of the Southern Dominion, trading its freedom from the Nether's houses for a place in his hosts.

events.name: The Thrall-Flight
events.summary: Three hundred thralls of Khorvazel steal boats and cross Veleeda to Olen, where the lamp-keepers shelter them; Khorvrath has demanded them back every year since.

countries.capitalReason: Khorvazel stands in the Nether foothills where the house first came up out of the Maw, close enough to the vent to feel its heat and far enough to keep its back to the Nether's houses.
countries.today: Lord Morvath rules the Nether foothills of the island from Khorvazel, perhaps 1,500 demons over some 35,000 thralls, orc and goblin labourers and men of the old coast. Khorvrath is the horned court of the Southern Dominion, it keeps its oath to Nafeher while Volgan's strength stands, and it still demands the return of the thralls who fled to Olen.

divergence.what: Khorvrath breaks its oath to Nafeher and seeks its own road when the Dominion falters.
divergence.consequence: A demon realm fights for itself on the island, and the Dominion's sworn realms begin to doubt their oaths.

divergence.what: Khorvrath raids Olen to take back its thralls.
divergence.consequence: The shrine-isle burns or holds, the freeholds learn that silence does not protect them, and Mirolon gains cause to strike first.

countries.name: Dolon

founding.story: A demon queen of the Nether came out with her house on the salt coast of the island in 2A 1120 and took the salt pans of the men who worked them, raising a pact-hall at Unzeky where the brine and the Maw's sulphur could both be had. Her house has kept the coast since, and the old accounts call her Khirara.

roots.story: The queens of Dolon rule by pact and write their laws in salt, and both customs come from the first of them. The house that became Dolon was a house of the Nether's Halls whose demons dealt in pacts with the living, the bargains that bind a mortal in service, obedience or tribute for life and end with him, because the dead are Zol's. In 2A 1120 its queen, whom the old accounts call Khirara, came up out of the Maw with her house onto the salt coast of the island and took the salt pans from the men who worked them; the coast tells that she drowned their headman in his own brine-pan and set on her head a ring of the salt crystals that grew on the pan's rim, which the heat of her body never melted. She raised the pact-hall of Unzeky over the brine pans, where the salt and the sulphur of the Maw could both be had, and her house has kept the coast since. From the salt crown come Dolon's laws: an oath of Dolon is written in salt, so that the sea can wash away any oath the queen regrets; the queen wears a crown of salt and is crowned in brine; and a thrall of the salt coast may buy his freedom only with a pact. The forge followed the pans. Since 4A 1651 Dolon's galleys have carried salt, sulphur and ash-glass to Nafeher as tribute, and since 4A 1693 the forges of Unzeky have compounded black powder from the coast's salts and the Maw's sulphur and armed Volgan's orc companies with powder-engines and casks. Queen Zhorith keeps the Dominion's forge.

sign.device: A crown of jagged white salt crystals, in salt white on obsidian black.
sign.origin: The salt crown is the crown of the first queen, the ring of brine crystals she took from the rim of the headman's pan, and the queens of Dolon have been crowned in brine and worn a crown of salt since 2A 1120. The house's banners have shown it since the pact-hall of Unzeky was raised, and the tribute galleys have flown it beneath the Gate of Nafeher along the Veshir coast since 4A 1651.
sign.meaning: Laws written in salt: to the thralls the promise that a pact can free them, and to every power that takes Dolon's oath the warning that the queen can let the sea wash it away.

dynasties.name: The House of the Salt Pact
dynasties.notable: The demon queens of Dolon, who rule by pact and write their laws in salt; the present queen, Zhorith, keeps the Dominion's forge.

events.name: The Queen's Coming
events.summary: Queen Khirara's house takes the salt coast of the island and raises the pact-hall of Unzeky over the brine pans.

events.name: The Tribute Galleys
events.summary: Dolon begins to send salt, sulphur and ash-glass to Nafeher in tribute galleys along the Veshir coast, and the Dominion's orders pay in thralls.

events.name: Dolon's Forge
events.summary: The forges of Unzeky compound black powder from the coast's salts and the Maw's sulphur, and Dolon begins to arm Volgan's orc companies with powder-engines and casks.

countries.capitalReason: Unzeky stands on the salt coast where the brine pans and the sulphur of the Nether Maw are both within reach, which is why the queen chose it for her pact-hall and why the forges stayed.
countries.today: Queen Zhorith rules the salt coast of the island from Unzeky, perhaps 1,200 demons over some 36,000 thralls and labourers. Dolon is the forge of the Southern Dominion: its black powder arms Volgan's orc companies, its galleys carry tribute along the Veshir coast, and its demons write their laws in salt so that the sea can wash away any oath the queen regrets.

divergence.what: Dolon sells powder to the freeholds or to the Dark Lands holds behind Nafeher's back.
divergence.consequence: Powder spreads to realms that Volgan does not control, and the Dominion's orc companies lose their edge.

divergence.what: A raid or an eruption destroys the forges of Unzeky.
divergence.consequence: Volgan's companies fight without powder, the Dominion's march is slower, and the sworn realms quarrel over the blame.

countries.name: Nezer

founding.story: In the Second Age the Nezer hills were Nazerun, the seat of the Great Necromancer Elzon, and when he died in Aenor his seat stood empty and its necromancers scattered. In 4A 3 two demon crowns of one family took the hills and the coast of the Sea of Nazerch, renamed them Nezer in their own speech and ruled them together from Gelroze.

roots.story: The two crowns of Nezer are a family of the Nether's ferrymen. In the Halls under Mount Nether their house kept the galleys that cross the Sea of Lava, the only ships that can, and its lords and queens were the steersmen of the Halls' trade with the surface. A galley of the lava sea has two steering oars, one at each quarter, and it holds its course only when both steersmen pull together, so the house has always been ruled by two of one blood. In the Second Age the Nezer hills were Nazerun, the seat of the Great Necromancer, and the coast of the Sea of Nazerch was his; the house ferried demons to the Burning Gate on the Nezer coast in the years of the portals and lost many when men, elves and Dark Lands soldiers closed the gate in 2A 1388. When the Necromancer died in Aenor his seat stood empty and his necromancers scattered, and in 4A 3 a queen and a lord of the ferrymen's house crossed the lava sea with their galleys, took the empty hills and the Nazerch coast, renamed them Nezer in their own speech and began to rule them together from Gelroze. From the galley come the crowns' customs: two crowns of one house rule and must agree on war; each crown keeps its own lands so that neither need cross the other's; and the trade with the Nether crosses the Sea of Lava on galleys that only demons sail. The crowns keep the Necromancer's hills and nothing of him, and they guard the broken ring of the Burning Gate on their coast. Nezer swore to Nafeher in 4A 1650, its two crowns agreeing for the first time in a century.

sign.device: A black galley with two steering oars at its stern, one at each quarter, in ember gold on nether red.
sign.origin: The two-oared galley is the lava galley of the ferrymen's house, the ship that holds its course only when both steersmen pull together. The queen and the lord who took the empty hills in 4A 3 crossed the Sea of Lava under it, and the twin crowns of Gelroze have flown it since; when the crowns disagree, the galley is flown with one oar shipped.
sign.meaning: Two crowns, one course: to the thralls and companies of Nezer the promise that the realm moves only when its crowns agree, and to Nafeher and the Nether the warning that the house that carries their trade can stop carrying it.

dynasties.name: The Twin Crowns of Gelroze
dynasties.notable: A confederacy of two demon crowns of one house, a queen and a lord who rule together and must agree on war; Queen Sathael and Lord Zeruath hold the crowns in 4A 1748.

events.name: The Necromancer's Seat
events.summary: Elzon makes Nazerun his seat after Dardan and directs from its hills the long war of raids against Aenor.

events.name: The Burning Gate Closed
events.summary: A garrison of men, a company of elves and Dark Lands soldiers close the Burning Gate, a portal of the Nether in a hold on the Nezer coast, and leave its broken ring standing.

events.name: The Empty Seat
events.summary: Elzon dies in Aenor; his seat at Nazerun stands empty, and its necromancers scatter to Nafeher or into the hills.

events.name: The Two Crowns
events.summary: Two demon crowns of one family take the empty hills and the Nazerch coast and name the realm Nezer.

events.name: Sworn to Nafeher
events.summary: Nezer swears to Volgan as a realm of the Southern Dominion, and its two crowns agree for the first time in a century.

countries.capitalReason: Gelroze is the hill-hold where the two crowns met when they took the empty seat of Nazerun, and it lies between the hills and the Nazerch coast, so that each crown can reach its own lands without crossing the other's.
countries.today: Queen Sathael and Lord Zeruath rule the Nezer hills and the coast of the Sea of Nazerch from Gelroze, perhaps 2,500 demons over some 70,000 thralls and labourers. Nezer is the largest of the sworn realms, it guards the broken ring of the Burning Gate on its coast, and its trade with the Nether crosses the Sea of Lava on galleys that only demons sail.

divergence.what: The two crowns disagree on the war and divide the realm.
divergence.consequence: Nezer fights itself, the Dominion loses its largest sworn realm, and the Nether is offered the half that refuses Nafeher.

divergence.what: The Burning Gate on the Nezer coast is opened again in the war years.
divergence.consequence: Demons pass to the surface in numbers, and the realms north of the Ember Lands face a threat their chronicles thought closed.

countries.name: Nether

founding.story: The Nether lies in the south of the Ember Lands, a volcanic island ringed by the Sea of Lava whose halls go down into the heat beneath it, and the court of its King of Demons is older than Volgan's conquest of Mirolon by the reckoning of its own houses. Nobody among men knows when the court began, and the houses count only the years of their pacts.

roots.story: The Nether is the oldest court of the demons in Aoaz and the seat of their king. Demons are corrupted angels, immortal Great Folk, and the houses of the Halls tell that when the first of them came down corrupted they went into the heat beneath the volcanic island ringed by the Sea of Lava, where nothing living could follow, and cut the Halls beneath Mount Nether. There they took one of themselves for king, the King of Demons, whose own name is not spoken among men, and they count only the years of their pacts. The court's order comes from the king's seal. A pact of the Nether is sealed when the king's seal, a five-pointed figure drawn in one unbroken line within a ring of fire, is burned into the bargain; the pact binds the living who make it, in service, obedience or tribute, and grants them real power in life, and when they die they are Zol's and not the king's, so the Halls take their price in life and nothing after. The houses compete for the king's favour and the right to open portals, and the house of the demon Agon is one of the oldest and least obedient. In the Second Age portals opened across Aoaz and demons raided Aenor, not all of them at Elzon's bidding; when the Burning Gate on the Nezer coast was closed in 2A 1388 and the houses quarrelled among themselves and with the Necromancer's order, the portals closed one by one, and by 3A 700 the Nether had withdrawn behind the Sea of Lava. Since 4A 1650 the king has sold companies of demons to Nafeher by bargain, renewed each reign and never sworn, and the Nether Maw is disputed with Volgan's servants.

sign.device: The King's seal: a five-pointed figure drawn in one unbroken line within a ring of fire, in pact gold on hall black.
sign.origin: The seal is the King of Demons' own sign, burned into every pact the Halls make with the living, and it is the only such figure on any banner of Aoaz. The houses of the Halls carry it above their own signs in every company the king sells to Nafeher, and a mortal who bears it burned into his skin is under a pact and may be touched by no house but the king's.
sign.meaning: Power in life, at a price: to those who seek the king the promise that the bargain is kept to the word, and to every house and every mortal the warning that the seal is never broken while the bargainer lives.

dynasties.name: The King of Demons and the Houses of the Halls
dynasties.notable: A monarchy of demonic houses under the King of Demons, whose own name is not spoken among men; the houses compete for his favour and the right to open portals, and the house of the demon Agon is one of the oldest and least obedient.

events.name: The Portal Raids
events.summary: Portals open across Aoaz, and demons of the Nether, the demon Agon among them, raid Aenor and other lands, not all of them at Elzon's bidding.

events.name: The Burning Gate Closed
events.summary: Men, elves and Dark Lands soldiers close the Burning Gate on the Nezer coast, and the houses of the Halls lose their nearest road to the surface.

events.name: The Closing of the Portals
events.summary: As the houses quarrel among themselves and with the Necromancer's order, the portals close one by one, and the Nether withdraws behind the Sea of Lava.

events.name: The First Bargain of the Age
events.summary: Envoys of Nafeher come to the Halls, and the King of Demons strikes a bargain with Volgan for companies of demons at a price, a bargain he renews each reign and never swears.

countries.capitalReason: Zarath-Nazur, the dark throne, is cut into the Halls under Mount Nether, where the heat is greatest and no mortal army can reach, and the king's court has never needed another reason.
countries.today: In 4A 1748 the King of Demons rules the Nether island and the Halls beneath it from Zarath-Nazur, some 6,000 demons of the houses, a handful of devils on the Burning Shore and about 30,000 thralls. The Nether keeps its own counsel: it sells companies to Nafeher by bargain, disputes the Nether Maw with Volgan's servants, and still answers those who know the old rites and pay its price, a pact that binds the living and ends with them, because the dead are Zol's.

divergence.what: The King of Demons refuses to renew the bargain with Nafeher.
divergence.consequence: Volgan marches without the Nether's companies, the Maw border becomes a war, and the sworn realms must choose between their oath and their kin.

divergence.what: A mortal ruler of the north seeks the king's pact in the war years.
divergence.consequence: The bargainer gains real power while he lives and pays in obedience or levies, and when he dies his heir is free, because the king does not take the dead.

countries.name: Halia

founding.story: The five salt freeholds of the peninsula's Veleeda coast, Mirodor, Mencnon, Bennen, Gelon and Dra, had each paid their own toll to whoever held the island since the First Age. In 4A 1655, when the storms changed and Nafeher's galleys came again, their headmen met at Halon and swore to pay one toll as one league, so that no freehold could be squeezed alone, and called the league Halia, the salt country.

roots.story: The salt freeholds of the Veleeda coast are the coast cousins of Mirolon, salt-boilers of the old Ainic tongue who worked the shore while the lake-folk built their kingdom, and their oldest custom is older than their shame. They boiled salt on the shore of Veleeda, the water their own speech calls the Dead's Sea, and they buried their dead in salt so that the sea air would not rot them. When Volgan came in 1A 1150 and his necromancers raised the dead of the lake-kingdom into his grave hosts, the freeholders believed they learned what their custom was for, because the dead they had buried quickly, deep and with salt did not rise. In 1A 1180, thirty years into Volgan's war, the coast cousins agreed to pay his tolls in salt and say nothing, and they were left to boil salt while the lake-kingdom burned. From that bargain come the freeholds' laws, which every child learns before it can work the pans: the dead are buried quickly and deep, with salt, and the dead man's oar or rake stands over the grave; nobody speaks of Volgan or of Zol at a grave; and a toll is paid to whoever holds the island and nothing more is said. For ages the five freeholds of Mirodor, Mencnon, Bennen, Gelon and Dra paid alone and were squeezed alone, until in 4A 1655, when the storms changed and Nafeher's galleys came again, their headmen met at Halon and swore to pay one toll as one league. The freeholds remember the thief who came along their coast going south and came back going north without growing older, but only in their taverns.

sign.device: An oar standing upright in a white cairn of salt, in oar brown and salt white on Veleeda grey.
sign.origin: The oar in the salt is the freeholds' grave: a fisher of the coast is buried deep and salted with his oar standing over him, and the freeholders believe the necromancers never raised a grave marked so. When the five freeholds swore their league at Halon in 4A 1655, each headman set his family's grave-oar in one heap of salt in the middle of the pans, and the league's banner has shown that oar since. It is the only sign on the peninsula that speaks of the dead, and it speaks of them without a word.
sign.meaning: Our dead are our own: to the freeholders a promise that the league will keep their graves salted and their silence paid, and to Nafeher the quiet reminder that the coast has kept its dead from it since the First Age.

dynasties.name: The Salt-Moot of Halon
dynasties.notable: The headmen of the five freeholds meet at Halon and choose a Moot-Headman for three years; Delen of Bennen speaks for the league in 4A 1748.

events.name: The Salted Graves
events.summary: When Volgan's necromancers raise the dead of the lake-kingdom into his grave hosts, the dead of the salt coast, buried quickly and deep with salt, do not rise, and the freeholders hold to their burial custom ever after.

events.name: Salt for Silence
events.summary: Thirty years into Volgan's war the coast cousins of Mirolon agree to pay his tolls in salt and say nothing, and they are left to boil salt while the lake-kingdom burns.

events.name: The Thief Came This Way
events.summary: The freeholders tell of a lone traveller from the north who came along their coast going south and, two years later, came back going north and did not seem to have grown any older.

events.name: The League of the Salt Coast
events.summary: The five freeholds swear at Halon to pay one toll as one league, and Nafeher accepts a single payment of salt and fish each year.

countries.capitalReason: Halon has the largest salt pans of the Veleeda coast and lies in the middle of the five freeholds, so the headmen could meet there without any of them travelling furthest.
countries.today: Moot-Headman Delen of Bennen speaks for the salt coast of the peninsula, some 355,000 salt-makers and fishers in five freeholds. Halia pays its salt to Nafeher for silence as its grandfathers did, trades fish and salt with Mirolon, its cousin, and remembers the thief who came this way, though only in its taverns.

divergence.what: The league shelters Mirolon's refugees and scouts when the Dominion comes.
divergence.consequence: Halia loses its silence and its peace, and the Dominion's march has an unwilling coast behind it.

divergence.what: The league kneels to Nafeher as a client crown.
divergence.consequence: Halia keeps its pans and loses its name, and the Dominion gains a harbour on the peninsula's south coast for the crossing to Mirolon.

countries.name: Nan

founding.story: The hill chieftains of the dark Nan Mountains and the isles beyond them fought each other for every cove until 4A 1188, when Feron the Grey, a chieftain who had learned the storm-pilots' route through the Tempest Reach, took the fort of Larorun and made the others swear to him as warlord. Nan has been ruled by the strongest captain of the mountains ever since.

roots.story: The hill-folk of the dark Nan Mountains are the men who ran from the gate. When Volgan's power first reached the old coast of the island in the First Age, the men of that coast who would not serve the Dominion took their boats across the storm belt to the southern tip of the peninsula and the isles beyond it, and hid in the mountains where the storms of the Tempest Reach break on the peaks. The storms that had nearly drowned them became their wall, and the families who learned to read the weather became the chieftains of the mountains. Their oldest wayfinders found that the storm-petrels, the small dark birds that fly low through the worst weather and seem to walk on the water, always know the gaps in a storm, and the wayfinders of Nan learned the storm-pilots' route through the Tempest Reach by following them. For ages the hill chieftains fought each other for every cove, until in 4A 1188 Feron the Grey, a chieftain who had learned the petrels' route, took the fort of Larorun and made the others swear to him as warlord; his chieftains named him for the grey of the storm, not of his hair. From the petrels' route come Nan's customs: the warlord is the captain the chieftains will follow and keeps the office only by success; the wayfinders' charts are secret, so that only Nan's pilots can bring a ship to the island and back; and a Nan pilot is sold to whoever pays most, Nafeher included. Almon the Small, a wayfinder from the southern isles, has held Larorun since 4A 1731.

sign.device: A dark storm-petrel skimming low with its wings bent, in storm black on grey.
sign.origin: The petrel is the bird the wayfinders of Nan followed through the Tempest Reach, the bird that knows the gaps in the storm. Feron the Grey flew a petrel banner from the mast of the ship that brought him through the storm to take Larorun in 4A 1188, and every warlord since has flown it over the fort; Nan's pilots wear a petrel feather in their caps, and a ship that carries one is under the warlord's protection, whoever has paid for it.
sign.meaning: The way through the storm: to the chieftains a promise that the warlord holds the only road, and to Mirolon and Nafeher alike the reminder that the road is for sale.

dynasties.name: The Warlords of Larorun
dynasties.notable: The warlord is the captain the hill chieftains will follow, chosen by acclamation and kept by success; Almon the Small, a wayfinder from the southern isles, has held Larorun since 4A 1731.

events.name: Feron Takes Larorun
events.summary: Feron the Grey takes the fort of Larorun and makes the chieftains of the Nan Mountains and the southern isles swear to him as warlord.

events.name: The Wayfinders' Charts
events.summary: The wayfinders of Nan chart the storm-pilots' route through the Tempest Reach and keep it secret, so that only Nan's pilots can bring a ship to the island and back.

events.name: The Raid on the Salt Coast
events.summary: A warlord of Nan raids the freeholds of the Veleeda coast for salt and slaves and is driven off by Mirolon's scouts, which the freeholds remember when they swear their league a century later.

events.name: The Toll to Nafeher
events.summary: When the Veil of Storms is raised, Nan's warlord agrees to pay a toll to Nafeher and to lend the Dominion his pilots, which his chieftains call good business.

countries.capitalReason: Larorun is the fort in the Nan Mountains that commands the southern tip of the peninsula and the coves of the isles, and whoever holds it holds the chieftains.
countries.today: Almon the Small rules the Nan Mountains and the southern isles from Larorun, a warlord's fort and some 59,000 hill-folk and islanders. Nan pays its toll to Nafeher, lends the Dominion its storm-pilots, and sells the same pilots to anyone who pays more, which makes it the one realm of the Ember Lands that both Mirolon and Nafeher need.

divergence.what: The warlord sells the storm-pilots' route to Mirolon or to Aenor.
divergence.consequence: A fleet of the north can reach the island through the Tempest Reach, and the Veil of Storms no longer hides the Dominion.

divergence.what: Nan swears to Nafeher as a realm of the Southern Dominion.
divergence.consequence: The Dominion gains the peninsula's southern tip and its pilots, and Mirolon is caught between the island and its own mountains.

countries.name: Olen

founding.story: In 2A 412 a breeze blew out of the storm belt for a whole winter and kept the lamps lit on the cliffs of the isle of Olen while every other light on the coast went out, and the fishers built a shrine where the breeze touched the cliff. The shrine's lamp-keepers became the isle's rulers, and the isle took the name of the Holy Breeze.

roots.story: The isle of Olen was a fishing isle under the storm belt, poor and dark, whose cliff lamps went out every winter when the storms came off the Tempest Reach. In 2A 412 a breeze blew out of the storm belt for a whole winter and kept the lamps lit on the cliffs of the isle while every other light on the coast went out, and the fishers saw sea-kestrels hanging still above the cliffs in that breeze, as if it held them up. They built a shrine where the kestrels hung, at Gelbus, and named the isle for the Holy Breeze, and the lamp-keepers of the shrine became the isle's rulers. The fishers believe the breeze came from beyond the storms as a sign that the isle is watched over, and the lamp-keepers do not say who watches. From the Holy Breeze come Olen's customs: the cliff lamps are kept lit through every storm; whoever reaches the cliffs out of the storm belt is sheltered and not asked where he came from; and the shrine is never moved from the place the breeze chose. The isle pays its toll to Nafeher like every coast of the peninsula and says nothing, but it has kept its shelter law even against the Dominion's sworn realms. In 4A 1712 three hundred thralls of Khorvrath stole boats and crossed Veleeda to Olen, and the lamp-keepers sheltered them and have refused every demand to give them back. The freehold of Luminor on the lamp-cliffs joined the shrine-realm in 4A 1590, and Olen holds the whole line of cliffs on the peninsula's south coast; its lamps are the first lights a ship sees coming out of the storm belt.

sign.device: A sea-kestrel hanging still in the air with its wings spread and its tail fanned, in cliff white on storm blue.
sign.origin: The hovering kestrel is the bird the fishers saw hanging in the Holy Breeze above the cliffs in the winter of 2A 412, where the shrine of Gelbus was built. The lamp-keepers carved it over the shrine door and have flown it from the lamp-cliffs since, and a refugee who reaches the cliffs is given a small cloth kestrel to wear, which every boat of Olen respects.
sign.meaning: Held up by the breeze: to whoever reaches its cliffs the promise of shelter, and to the Dominion's sworn realms the isle's refusal to give back what the breeze has brought.

dynasties.name: The Lamp-Keepers of Gelbus
dynasties.notable: The keepers of the cliff lamps govern the isle as a shrine-realm, choosing a First Keeper from among themselves; Helia of the Lamps is First Keeper in 4A 1748.

events.name: The Holy Breeze
events.summary: A breeze out of the storm belt keeps the cliff lamps of Olen lit through a whole winter, and the shrine of the Holy Breeze is built at Gelbus.

events.name: The Union with Luminor
events.summary: The freehold of Luminor on the lamp-cliffs joins the shrine-realm, and Olen holds the whole line of cliffs on the peninsula's south coast.

events.name: The Shelter of the Thrall-Flight
events.summary: The lamp-keepers shelter three hundred thralls who fled Khorvrath across Veleeda and refuse every demand to give them back.

countries.capitalReason: Gelbus is the shrine-town on the cliff where the Holy Breeze touched the isle, and the keepers will not move the shrine from the place the breeze chose.
countries.today: First Keeper Helia of the Lamps governs the isle of the Holy Breeze, the lamp-cliffs and Luminor from Gelbus, some 237,000 fishers and pilgrims. Olen pays its toll to Nafeher and shelters whoever reaches its cliffs, including the thralls Khorvrath still demands, and its lamps are the first lights a ship sees coming out of the storm belt.

divergence.what: The keepers hand back the thralls to buy Khorvrath's peace.
divergence.consequence: Olen keeps its cliffs and loses its name as a refuge, and the freeholds learn that the Holy Breeze can be bought.

divergence.what: Olen lights its lamps in Mirolon's beacon code.
divergence.consequence: Mirolon sees the island's fleets a day earlier, and Olen becomes a target of the Dominion.

cities.name: Nafeher
cities.economy: The gate and halls of the Dominion; the necromantic orders; the grave-fields
cities.legend: Volgan's orcs say that nobody comes back up from the Abyss except the one who stole from it, and that the gate of Nafeher was shut on the day he came back.

cities.name: Miherta
cities.economy: Lake fish, timber, marsh grain and reed paper; the wardens' seat
cities.legend: The wardens say the old lake-kings' crown hangs in the beacon tower of Miherta and that it will be worn again on the night the beacons are no longer needed.

cities.name: Borpial
cities.economy: The fort of the northern passes; the scouts' muster
cities.legend: The scouts say the north gate was built in one summer by every warden-family carrying a stone, and that the stones of families who failed to come lie in a heap beside it.

cities.name: Khorvazel
cities.economy: Thrall labour, obsidian and sulphur; the horned court
cities.legend: The thralls say the horns over the gate of Khorvazel belong to beasts that came up out of the Maw with the house, and that they grow back when they are broken.

cities.name: Unzeky
cities.economy: Salt pans, sulphur and the powder forges of the Dominion
cities.legend: The salt-workers say that the queens of Dolon write their oaths in salt on the beach at low tide, so that the sea can carry off any promise the queen regrets.

cities.name: Gelroze
cities.economy: Hill farms of the thralls; the galley trade across the Sea of Lava
cities.legend: The thralls of the Nezer hills say that the Necromancer's chair still stands in the empty hall of Nazerun, and that neither crown of Gelroze will sit in it.

cities.name: Zarath-Nazur
cities.economy: Pact-tribute, thrall labour in the obsidian galleries, fire-glass
cities.legend: Men of the south say that the Throne of Embers is carved from a single stone that was cool when the king first sat on it, and that the Halls have been growing hotter ever since.

cities.name: Halon
cities.economy: The largest salt pans of the Veleeda coast; fish
cities.legend: The freeholders say that a thief once came through their coast going south and, years later, came back going north and did not grow older, and that he paid for his bread in coin nobody had seen before.

cities.name: Larorun
cities.economy: Hill herds, the storm-pilots' fees, raiding when the warlord allows it
cities.legend: The hill-folk say that Feron the Grey learned the route through the Tempest Reach from a drowned pilot who spoke to him from the water, and that every warlord since has been taught it by the one before.

cities.name: Gelbus
cities.economy: Pilgrims, fish and the tallow of the cliff lamps
cities.legend: The lamp-keepers say the Holy Breeze still blows on the cliff of Gelbus on the night of every great storm, and that a lamp lit there in that breeze cannot be put out by any wind of the Reach.

figures.name: Mirena of the Passes
figures.biography: A scout-master of the northern passes who was elected High Warden in 4A 1739, she reads every report from the south herself, has doubled the beacon line along the Sound, and has stopped expecting help from Parim.

figures.name: Baelan of Paron
figures.biography: The envoy who warned the court at Parim in 4A 1736 that the Ember Lands were arming and was laughed out of the hall; he has written down every word the courtiers said to him and reads them aloud to new scouts.

figures.name: Hadric of Miherta
figures.biography: A lake-town captain who led the survivors back from the Great Swamp after Dardan and was chosen the first High Warden; he refused to wear the lake-kings' crown and hung it in the beacon tower instead.

figures.name: Feron the Grey
figures.biography: The hill chieftain who learned the storm-pilots' route through the Tempest Reach, took Larorun and made the chieftains of the Nan Mountains swear to him; his chieftains named him for the grey of the storm, not of his hair.

lawsAndCustoms.name: Salt for silence
lawsAndCustoms.summary: The freeholds of the peninsula pay a yearly toll in salt and fish to whoever holds the island and say nothing of Volgan or of Zol at the grave; they bury their dead quickly and deep, with salt.

lawsAndCustoms.name: The beacon law
lawsAndCustoms.summary: Every warden tower of Mirolon keeps a lamp lit toward the south each night, and a warden who lets his lamp go out is struck from the rolls; the High Warden is elected for life and may not pass the office to a child.

lawsAndCustoms.name: Pact-names
lawsAndCustoms.summary: Every demon lord or queen keeps a name of two beats for the world and a pact-name that only the pact knows; oaths are made in blood and ash, and in Dolon they are written in salt.

lawsAndCustoms.name: The lava rite
lawsAndCustoms.summary: Devils are bound to their bodies and can be killed, and a slain devil returns only when its skull is thrown into lava; who performs the rite for the devils who serve the Dominion is not known outside Nafeher.

lawsAndCustoms.name: The king's pacts
lawsAndCustoms.summary: The King of Demons can be called on by the old rites and grants real power in life; the bargain binds the living who make it, in service, obedience or tribute, and when they die they are Zol's, not his.
